mathematical_contract.authority: the two original bivariate equations are specialized into the selected local algebraic field before their actual fiber degrees are inspected
mathematical_contract.field: rational-polynomial fractions are reduced modulo the retained parameter's defining polynomial; exact isolator evidence selects the intended real root even when that polynomial is reducible
mathematical_contract.fiber: the exact local-field polynomial GCD of the specialized authored equations is the single common-fiber authority
mathematical_contract.root_counter: a square-free local-field Sturm sequence counts distinct common roots in the candidate isolator, including even-multiplicity and exact endpoint roots
mathematical_contract.zero_equations: if exactly one specialized equation is zero, the other equation supplies the fiber; if both are zero, the fiber is positive-dimensional and is reported explicitly
fast_path_order: specialized common-fiber GCD and Sturm count in both orientations
mathematical_contract.acceptance: Counted(0) rejects the projected pair, Counted(n>0) accepts exact Direct evidence, and an identically zero common fiber returns Boundary uncertainty rather than inventing a point
mathematical_contract.strict: STRICT uses only exact identities, rational arithmetic, certified algebraic isolators, exact local-field GCD, and exact Sturm variation
mathematical_contract.approximate_512: APPROXIMATE_512 follows the same proof graph; approximation is permitted only when an inherited Hyperlimit sign/equality reaches its 512-bit terminal, and consumed approximate certainty is propagated
mathematical_contract.unsupported: unsupported coefficient towers remain Predicate uncertainty; positive-dimensional components are retained as Boundary uncertainty for overlap classification
mathematical_contract.no_predicates_build: without the optional predicate backend, unresolved decisions remain explicit Incomplete/Predicate evidence and never become floating contacts

canonical_degree_drop_fixture.property: specialization deletes the formal leading A*B term in either orientation while the exact common fiber retains beta=alpha^2

completion_change.before: Hypercurve rejected specialized degree drops conservatively and carried separate positive-index subresultant reports plus endpoint-sign and local-Sturm fallbacks
completion_change.after: one specialization-first common-GCD engine handles stable degree, degree drop, and even multiplicity without interpolated subresultant reports
completion_change.false_positive_guard: a degree-drop projection whose only apparent solution is a root at infinity is rejected by a zero finite-root count
completion_change.positive_dimension_guard: two equations that both vanish on the selected fiber return explicit Boundary uncertainty
completion_change.test_matrix: both orientations and both STRICT/APPROXIMATE_512 policies cover degree drop, even multiplicity, rootless fibers, fully vanished fibers, and reducible field carriers
